arxiv-1704-06810.title: Structures of Nichols (braided) Lie algebras of diagonal type
arxiv-1704-06810.creator: Weicai Wu, Jing Wang, Shouchuan Zhang and Yao-Zhong Zhang
arxiv-1704-06810.description: Abstract Let V V be a braided vector space of diagonal type. Let 𝔅 ⁡ ( V ) \mathfrak{B}(V) , 𝔏 − ​ ( V ) \mathfrak{L}^{-}(V) and 𝔏 ⁡ ( V ) \mathfrak{L}(V) be the Nichols algebra, Nichols Lie algebra and Nichols braided Lie algebra over V V , respectively.

arxiv-2101-06315.title: A Multi-Platform Study of Crowd Signals Associated with Successful Online Fundraising
arxiv-2101-06315.creator: Henry K. Dambanemuya, Emőke-Ágnes Horvát
arxiv-2101-06315.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Henry K. Dambanemuya, Emőke-Ágnes Horvát. The growing popularity of online fundraising (aka “crowdfunding”) has attracted significant research on the subject. In contrast to previous studies that attempt to predict the success of crowdfunded projects based on specific characteristics of the projects and their creators, we present a more general approach that focuses on crowd dynamics and is robust to the particularities of different crowdfunding platforms.

arxiv-2104-06321.title: Does our universe conform with the existence of a universal maximum energy-density ρ m ​ a ​ x u ​ n ​ i \rho^{uni}_{max} ?
arxiv-2104-06321.creator: Hujeirat A.A
arxiv-2104-06321.description: Abstract Recent astronomical observations of high redshift quasars, dark matter-dominated galaxies, mergers of neutron stars, glitch phenomena in pulsars, cosmic microwave background and experimental data from hadronic colliders do not rule out, but they even support the hypothesis that the energy-density in our universe most likely is upper-limited by ρ m ​ a ​ x u ​ n ​ i

arxiv-2105-00601.title: Maximum Principle Preserving Finite Difference Scheme for 1-D Nonlocal-to-Local Diffusion Problems
arxiv-2105-00601.creator: Amanda Gute, Xingjie Helen Li
arxiv-2105-00601.description: Abstract In a recent paper [ 7 ] , a quasi-nonlocal coupling method was introduced to seamlessly bridge a nonlocal diffusion model with the classical local diffusion counterpart in a one-dimensional space. The proposed coupling framework removes interfacial inconsistency, preserves the balance of fluxes, and satisfies the maximum principle of diffusion problem.

arxiv-2202-04898.title: Nanostructured transition metal dichalcogenide multilayers for advanced nanophotonics
arxiv-2202-04898.creator: Battulga Munkhbat, Betül Küçüköz, Denis G. Baranov, Tomasz J. Antosiewicz, Timur O. Shegai
arxiv-2202-04898.description: Abstract Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) attract significant attention due to their exceptional optical, excitonic, mechanical, and electronic properties. Nanostructured multilayer TMDs were recently shown to be highly promising for nanophotonic applications, as motivated by their exceptionally high refractive indexes and optical anisotropy.

arxiv-2206-07543.title: P-Index
arxiv-2206-07543.creator: Shiva P. Pudasaini
arxiv-2206-07543.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Shiva P. Pudasaini. Abstract: I propose the P-Index that genuinely constitutes a well-defined, compact author citation metric. Significance: By considering the actual author contributions, the P-Index comprehensively resolves the question of true author citation measure. The P-Index brings a complete overhaul in our perception of the author citation metric, including total citations, from which the researchers and authors greatly benefit with compact measures.

arxiv-2302-14102.title: Connectivity Optimized Nested Graph Networks for Crystal Structures
arxiv-2302-14102.creator: Robin Ruff, Patrick Reiser, Jan Stühmer, Pascal Friederich
arxiv-2302-14102.description: Abstract Graph neural networks (GNNs) have been applied to a large variety of applications in materials science and chemistry. Here, we recapitulate the graph construction for crystalline (periodic) materials and investigate its impact on the GNNs model performance. We suggest the asymmetric unit cell as a representation to reduce the number of atoms by using all symmetries of the system.

arxiv-2305-15160.title: Dopant-assisted stabilization of negatively charged single nitrogen-vacancy centers in phosphorus-doped diamond at low temperatures
arxiv-2305-15160.creator: Jianpei Geng, Tetyana Shalomayeva, Mariia Gryzlova, Amlan Mukherjee, Santo Santonocito, Dzhavid Dzhavadzade, Durga Dasari, Hiromitsu Kato, Rainer Stöhr, Andrej Denisenko, Norikazu Mizuochi, Jörg Wrachtrup
arxiv-2305-15160.description: Abstract Charge state instabilities have been a bottleneck for the implementation of solid-state spin systems and pose a major challenge to the development of spin-based quantum technologies. Here we investigate the stabilization of negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy (NV - ) centers in phosphorus-doped diamond at liquid helium temperatures.

arxiv-2401-04477.title: Heisenberg homology of ribbon graphs
arxiv-2401-04477.creator: Christian Blanchet
arxiv-2401-04477.description: Abstract We review Heisenberg homology of configurations in once bounded surfaces and extend the construction to the regular thickening of a finite graph with ribbon structure. 2020 MSC : 57K20, 55R80, 55N25, 20C12 Key words : Mapping class group, monodromy, configuration spaces, ribbon graphs, Heisenberg homology.

arxiv-2511-21470.title: A PTR polynomial for the Hughes planes and a new class of permutation polynomials involving Catalan numbers
arxiv-2511-21470.creator: Stephen Brittain, Robert S. Coulter, Alice Man Wa Hui
arxiv-2511-21470.description: Abstract . Hughes introduced the projective planes that bear his name in 1957 and they have since been studied extensively. However, until now, no polynomial representation of a planar ternary ring that represents them has been determined. In this paper, we rectify this omission by determining a reduced PTR polynomial for any Hughes plane defined over a regular nearfield.

europmc-pmc2481392.title: Temperature-dependent sex determination in fish revisited: prevalence, a single sex ratio response pattern, and possible effects of climate change.
europmc-pmc2481392.creator: Ospina-Alvarez N, Piferrer F.
europmc-pmc2481392.description: Background In gonochoristic vertebrates, sex determination mechanisms can be classified as genotypic (GSD) or temperature-dependent (TSD). Some cases of TSD in fish have been questioned, but the prevalent view is that TSD is very common in this group of animals, with three diffe

plos-pone-0001822.title: Song Diversity Predicts the Viability of Fragmented Bird Populations
plos-pone-0001822.creator: Paola Laiolo, Matthias Vögeli, David Serrano et al.
plos-pone-0001822.description: PLOS ONE research article. In the global scenario of increasing habitat fragmentation, finding appropriate indicators of population viability is a priority for conservation. We explored the potential of learned behaviours, specifically acoustic signals, to predict the persistence over time of fragmented bi

pmc-10511190.title: Optical force brush enabled free-space painting of 4D functional structures
pmc-10511190.creator: Chenqi Yi, Shuyuan Qu, Yaoyu Wang, Haoning Qi, Yufeng Zhang, Gary J. Cheng
pmc-10511190.description: Femtosecond laser–based technique called two-photon polymerization (TPP) has emerged as a powerful tool for nanofabrication and integrating nanomaterials. However, challenges persist in existing three-dimensional (3D) nanoprinting methods, such as slow layer-by-layer printing and limited material options due to laser-matter interactions. Here, we present an approach to 3D nanoprinting called free-space nanopainting, using an optical force brush (OFB).

pmc-11360023.title: Ligand Shell Thickness of PEGylated Gold Nanoparticles Controls Cellular Uptake and Radiation Enhancement
pmc-11360023.creator: Paul T. Lawrence, Avery S. Daniels, Allison J. Tierney, E. Charles H. Sykes, Charles R. Mace
pmc-11360023.description: The drive to improve the safety and efficacy of radiotherapies for cancers has prompted the development of nanomaterials that can locally amplify the radiation dose at a tumor without damaging the surrounding healthy tissue. Gold nanoparticles (Au NPs), in particular, exhibit promising radiosensitizing properties under kilovolt X-ray exposure, although the precise mechanism behind this enhancement is not fully understood.

pmc-11367145.title: Artificial intelligence algorithms permits rapid acute kidney injury risk classification of patients with acute myocardial infarction
pmc-11367145.creator: Jun Wei, Dabei Cai, Tingting Xiao, Qianwen Chen, Wenwu Zhu, Qingqing Gu, Yu Wang, Qingjie Wang, Xin Chen, Shenglin Ge, Ling Sun
pmc-11367145.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to develop and validate several artificial intelligence (AI) models to identify acute myocardial infarction (AMI) patients at an increased risk of acute kidney injury (AKI) during hospitalization.MethodsIncluded were patients diagnosed with AMI from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC) III and IV databases.

pmc-11590350.title: Puberty and NeuroDevelopment in adolescents (PANDA): a study protocol
pmc-11590350.creator: Katherine O Bray, Olivia Durbin, Stephanie Hartanto, Muskan Khetan, Daniel Liontos, Sarah J Manuele, Isabel Zwaan, Despina Ganella, Megan M Herting, Jee Hyun Kim, Michele O’Connell, Elena Pozzi, Orli Schwartz, Marc Seal, Julian Simmons, Nandita Vijayakumar, Sarah Whittle
pmc-11590350.description: BackgroundBiopsychosocial changes during adolescence are thought to confer risk for emotion dysregulation, and in particular, anxiety disorders. However, there are substantial gaps in our knowledge about the biological mechanisms underlying anxiety during adolescence, and whether this contributes to the higher prevalence in females.

pmc-11613475.title: Integration of psychological interventions in multi-sectoral humanitarian programmes: a systematic review
pmc-11613475.creator: Jacqueline N Ndlovu, Jonna Lind, Andrés Barrera Patlán, Nawaraj Upadhaya, Marx R Leku, Josephine Akellot, Morten Skovdal, Jura L Augustinavicius, Wietse A Tol
pmc-11613475.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundEvery year, millions of people are affected by humanitarian crises. With a growing population of people affected, the need for coordination and integration of services aiming to improve the effectiveness of mental health and psychosocial support also grows. In this study, we examine how psychological interventions in humanitarian settings globally have been implemented through integration into programming outside of formal healthcare delivery through multisectoral integration.MethodsA comprehensive search of six databases and reference checking was undertaken in 2022.

pmc-11614513.title: Long Noncoding RNA EMX2-AS Facilitates Osteoblast Differentiation and Bone Formation by Inhibiting EMX2 Protein Translation and Activating Wnt/β-Catenin Pathway
pmc-11614513.creator: Linyuan Fan, Li Zhang, Xin Zhang, Wei Wei, Zhaohui Liu
pmc-11614513.description: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs), as a potentially new and crucial element of biological regulation, have gained widespread attention in recent years. Our previous work identified lncRNA empty spiracles homeobox 2 antisence (EMX2-AS) was significantly increased during the osteoblast differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs).

pmc-11644996.title: Improving Circulating Tumor Cell Detection Using Image Synthesis and Transformer Models in Cancer Diagnostics
pmc-11644996.creator: Shuang Liang, Xue Bai, Yu Gu
pmc-11644996.description: Cancer is the second leading cause of death, significantly threatening human health. Effective treatment options are often lacking in advanced stages, making early diagnosis crucial for reducing mortality rates. Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) are a promising biomarker for early detection; however, their automatic detection is challenging due to their heterogeneous size and shape, as well as their scarcity in blood.

pmc-11716615.title: Changes in peripheral AD biomarkers in a randomized controlled trial of Yoga vs. memory training in older women at risk for Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-11716615.creator: Helen Lavretsky
pmc-11716615.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundBiomarkers such as amyloid beta (Aβ) peptides and tau protein can correlate with changes in cognition and mood symptoms associated with AD. We aimed to investigate the blood biomarker response to a Kundalini Yoga (KY) compared to Memory Enhancement Training (MET) intervention as well as determine the predictive value of blood biomarkers on outcomes in a randomized trial targeting women at risk for Alzheimer's disease.MethodWomen aged 60 years old and older with subjective memory complaints and high cardiovascular risk score were randomized

pmc-12387698.title: Evaluation of iStent Micro-Bypass vs. Kahook Dual Blade Goniotomy with Phacoemulsification in Open-Angle Glaucoma: A Systematic Review
pmc-12387698.creator: Anna Charytonowicz, Jakub Błażowski, Joanna Konopińska, Eun Ji Lee
pmc-12387698.description: Background/Objectives: Glaucoma refers to a group of eye diseases that damage the optic nerve, causing irreversible vision loss. It typically begins with peripheral vision impairment and, in severe cases, leads to complete blindness. A major advancement in glaucoma treatment is Microinvasive Glaucoma Surgery (MIGS), including trabecular bypass and ab interno trabeculectomy, which are generally used for mild to moderate glaucoma.

pmc-12573552.title: Treating complex PTSD with Schema Therapy, ImRs and EMDR: a review and case study
pmc-12573552.creator: Mellony T.C. van Hemert, Paula M. de Jong, Tessa R. Brouwer, Luciano Zoon, Ellen Gunst, Laurence Claes, Manuel Morrens
pmc-12573552.description: Introduction: Complex PTSD (CPTSD) often results from prolonged trauma, such as childhood abuse or domestic violence. Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) and Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) are recommended for treating PTSD. However, their limited effectiveness for CPTSD highlights the need for alternatives such as Schema Therapy (ST) and Imagery Rescripting.

pmc-12630620.title: Digital supply chain transformation improves corporate carbon emission efficiency in Chinese listed companies
pmc-12630620.creator: Jiangying Wei, Xiuwu Zhang, Yingtian Cheng
pmc-12630620.description: Supply chain digitalization presents significant potential for aligning economic growth with environmental sustainability; however, the mechanisms through which it enhances carbon emission efficiency remain insufficiently explored in emerging economies. This study investigates the impact of digital transformation on corporate carbon performance in China, utilizing the Supply Chain Innovation and Application Pilot Initiative as a quasi-natural experiment.

pmc-12713017.title: A Modern Roman‐Inspired Concrete with Daytime Radiative Cooling Capacity
pmc-12713017.creator: Jorge S. Dolado, Guido Goracci, Ghizlane Moutaoukil, Ridwan O. Agbaoye, Miguel Beruete, Alicia E. Torres‐García, Laura Carlosena, Achutha Prabhu, Jose A. Ibáñez, Nick Adams, Nicole van Lipzig, Karen Allacker
pmc-12713017.description: Addressing global warming through the modernization of buildings and urban areas is a major challenge. Passive daytime radiative cooling (PDRC) materials offer potential solutions, but none have effectively replaced concrete's dominant role in urban environments. Here, a Roman‐inspired concrete with PDRC capabilities is presented, combining high solar reflectance (≈0.95) and long‐wave infrared (LWIR) emittance (≈0.91).

pmc-13036892.title: Determinants and strategies influencing implementation of a clinically integrated breastfeeding peer counseling program: an application of the Implementation Research Logic Model
pmc-13036892.creator: Lauren S Keenan-Devlin, Ann E B Borders, Tricia J Johnson, Lisa R Hirschhorn
pmc-13036892.description: BackgroundBreastmilk feeding improves long term health outcomes, but few mother-infant dyads in the US meet recommendations, and breastfeeding duration is lowest for racially minoritized populations. Clinically integrated Breastfeeding Peer Counseling (ci-BPC) is an evidence-based practice that has been associated with improved breastfeeding outcomes for minoritized populations, but implementation evidence is limited.

pmc-13331162.title: Outcomes in spinal ependymoma: A retrospective analysis of 38 patients
pmc-13331162.creator: Khaled Badran, Daniel Robinson, Amjad Ali, Muhammad Dherijha
pmc-13331162.description: Background: Spinal ependymomas are rare central nervous system tumors with an incidence of approximately 1 in 100,000. They comprise 2–6% of CNS tumors, and up to 60% of intramedullary tumors. In this study, we retrospectively analyzed prognostic factors affecting progression-free survival (PFS) and postoperative outcomes for 38 patients.

pmc-13355227.title: Broad reverse approach surgery for hidradenitis suppurativa (BRASH): An inside-out surgical technique for localized hidradenitis suppurativa
pmc-13355227.creator: Giulio Gualdi, Davide Bertolla, Fabrizio Panarese, Ludovica Ucci, Patrick Silvetti, Leonardo Balestra, Giuditta Trobbiani, Paolo Amerio
pmc-13355227.description: lthough medical therapy is essential to control inflammation, surgery is often required for persistent localized tunnelized lesions unlikely to resolve pharmacologically. Standard surgical approaches, most commonly deroofing or excision, typically address the disease from the surface inward.1,2 In selected cases requiring wider excision and reconstruction, skin grafts or dermal substitutes may be needed, increasing complexity, costs, and resource use.

pmc-13672748.title: Burnout and psychosocial working conditions in a multidisciplinary hospital radiology team: a cross-sectional study using the job demands–resources framework
pmc-13672748.creator: Thomas Dertnig, Patrick Kutschar, Hans-Peter Wiesinger
pmc-13672748.description: ObjectivesBurnout is a major concern in hospital radiology, but data on psychosocial work conditions remain limited. Using the job demands–resources (JD–R) framework, this study examined burnout and its associations with psychosocial work factors across professional groups in a German university hospital radiology department.Materials and methodsAn exploratory cross-sectional survey was conducted among radiologists and non-physician staff.
